questions.question: A can finish a piece of work in a certain number of days. B takes 45% more number of days to finish the same work independently. They worked together for 58 days and then the remaining work was done by B alone in 29 days. In how many days could A have completed the work, had he worked alone?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

B takes 45% more number of days to finish the same work independently.

They worked together for 58 days and then the remaining work was done by B alone in 29 days.

**Formula:**

Total work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

Let number of days taken by A to complete the work be 100 days

Number of days taken by B to complete the work = 100 × (145/100) = 145

Time ratio of A to that of B = 100 : 145 = 20 : 29

Efficiency ratio of A to that of B = 29 : 20

Let efficiency of A = 29 unit/day

Efficiency of B = 20 unit/day

Work done by A and B in 58 days = (29 + 20) × 58 = 49 × 58 = 2842 unit

Remaining work which is done by B in 29 days = 20 × 29 = 580 unit

Total work = 2842 + 580 = 3422 unit

∴ Time taken by A to complete the whole work = 3422/29 = 118

• The dance developed and grew within the Satras, it is named after these religious institutions.

questions.question: How many parathyroid glands are present on the back side of the thyroid gland in humans?

• Hormones are sent to the different parts of the body through blood plasma.
 
• Example: **Pituitary gland, Thyroid gland.**

__
 
• **Karl Landsteiner **discovered human blood groups in the year **1900.**
 
• The discovery laid the foundation for the modern medical practice of blood transfusion.
 
• Karl Landsteiner**​**__ himself considered it an accidental discovery.
 
• On the basis of the presence of **Antigen or Glycoprotein, **there are four groups of blood in human:
 __
 
• That contains Antigen A–Blood **Group A.**
 
• That contains Antigen B–Blood **Group B.**
 
• That contains **both the Antigens A and B**–Blood **Group AB.**
 
• That contains **neither of the Antigens**– Blood **Group O.**
 
 
 
• Blood **Group O** is called the **Universal Donor.**
 
• Blood **Group AB** is called** Universal Receptor.​**
